storyboard.claim: The criticism measures the novel against a traditional chronological Victorian novel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon, the standard the critics are holding Beloved against.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the segment on the common criticism of the book's structure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the yardstick being used, not the verdict on it.

storyboard.claim: The confusion the critics complain about is intended by the author.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame: the reversal of the critics' complaint.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pushes back on the criticism just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the complaint into the book's design.

storyboard.claim: The novel's form follows trauma, which does not run in a straight line.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from trauma to circular time instead of a straight timeline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the confusion is structural.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the neat chronological form with the circular one.

storyboard.claim: Trauma is circular and it collapses time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame carrying the claim; no icon fits a circular collapse of time without reading as a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the principle behind the flow diagram.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the idea of memory as a place, which the next beat develops.

storyboard.claim: Remembering is a place: going back to where something terrible happened means it is still happening there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe in the kitchen of 124 Bluestone Road, the house as the place where the past stays.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the abstract idea of circular trauma to a concrete place.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the house itself the memory that refuses to end.

callout.text: We have to lose our footing

storyboard.claim: The reader must feel the same disorientation as the characters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame: the reader's experience, not a character's.
storyboard.onScreenText: We have to lose our footing
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the analysis from the book's form to the reader.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the confusion as the method that lets us understand Sethe and Paul D.

callout.text: No neat date on a haunting

storyboard.claim: Sethe and Paul D cannot organize their lives chronologically, because the past will not be dated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul D and Sethe together in the kitchen, both troubled and unable to settle on one time.
storyboard.onScreenText: No neat date on a haunting
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the characters caught in the disorientation just described.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the haunting as the reason no chronology holds.

storyboard.claim: The trauma is always present tense for the characters, so the book is written in present tense for the reader.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, still, thinking; the frame holds the present moment of her trauma.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects the characters' experience to the narrative choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the technique: Morrison puts the reader inside the present of the trauma.

storyboard.claim: The chokecherry scar on Sethe's back works as a receipt, the book's central record of the debt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree icon for the chokecherry scar, with Sethe in the kitchen as its bearer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recaps the book's images of accounting, from the house to the scar.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the scar from a wound into a ledger entry; the tree is literal, the scar is on her back.

storyboard.claim: Sethe refused to count her love in fractions; the narrator rejects the arithmetic of love.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe, still and sad, with the rejected phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the recap of images and names the mother's refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the phrase as rejected, not as a claim about the mother.

callout.text: The grave over the bill of sale

storyboard.claim: Sethe chose the grave over the bill of sale; in a world that counts people as property, she made a choice the book asks us to weigh.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon, the literal reading of the choice, with Sethe thinking beside it.
storyboard.onScreenText: The grave over the bill of sale
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the recap of images to the central choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the choice as the book's accounting; no violence is staged.

storyboard.claim: In a world that counts people as fractions, the only way to become whole is to do the unthinkable math yourself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-led frame addressing the viewer; the arithmetic is the viewer's own task.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the choice to the reader.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the analysis's final demand explicit: the reader must do the accounting.

storyboard.claim: Sethe chose a grave over a bill of sale, and the math was impossible, but she did it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sethe slumped in grief, carrying the weight of the impossible choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the segment on the mother's choice and the cost of it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Holds the grief of the choice without staging any harm.
